data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Chile factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Chile performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably comparing 2022 to 2018 and earlier waves). The assessment uses two hour-long tests with different students receiving different item combinations, and students also complete a background questionnaire; OECD reports mean scores, proficiency levels (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and distributional comparisons such as gaps between top and bottom performers. For Chile, average performance is described as broadly similar to 2018, with mathematics below 2015 and science stable over 2006–2022. The factsheet also reports within-country equity patterns (e.g., socioeconomic divides measured via ESCS), gender differences, and immigrant-background gaps, alongside contextual indicators such as belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences. It is a descriptive reporting product and does not provide an ML modeling evaluation or a reproducible predictive pipeline.
